newsitem.title: USA: Freight train derails near Fresno, Calif.
newsitem.headline: Freight train derails near Fresno, Calif.

text.p: A freight train carrying some hazardous materials derailed early Sunday south of Fresno, Calif., causing no injuries but forcing local authorities to seal off the area.

The Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp freight train derailed at 4:19 a.m. local time in a remote area about 10 miles south of Fresno. The train was traveling about 60 miles per hour at the time. The cause was under investigation.

Fifteen of the freight cars derailed, causing trailers and containers to split open. There were some hazardous materials on the board, including paint, batteries, some pesticides and compressed gas cylinders, the company said.
"Obviously everytime there are hazardous materials involved it's serious. However, these were relatively small quantities," Burlington Northern Santa Fe spokesman Mike Martin said.

The derailment forced the closure of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe line, which runs from Bakersfield to the San Francisco Bay Area. The line handles about 20 freight and eight passenger trains per day.
The rail line is Burlington Northern Santa Fe's only Central Valley link from southern to northern California. It was unclear when the line would reopen, Martin said.
Local authorities said there were no injuries but that they were forced to evacuate three nearby family homes.
"We sealed off the area," said Lt. Don Burk of the Fresno sheriff's department. "Three families were evacuated."
A Burlington Northern Santa Fe hazardous materials team was assembling at the scene to work with local authorities.
Burk said firefighters were standing by.
